newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly down.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover rose to 2.30 billion yuan from last Friday's 1.177 billion yuan with the 60-day contract the most active.
Banks from Dalian and Beijing were the main sellers on the market because they had excessive money after the central bank banned banks from trading state treasury bills, traders said.
They said non-banking financial institutions borrowed money for trading on the stock market.
"The rates (on the interbank market) are lower than those on the repurchase market, so the institutions are willing to borrow on the interbank market," one trader said.
Traders said they were still waiting for the confirmation of rumours that the central bank would shortly cut bank reserve ratios.
